question: Which three economies topped the IMD World Competitiveness Ranking in June 2025?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Switzerland, Singapore, and Hong Kong**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **IMD World Competitiveness Ranking**, released in **June 2025**, identifies the most competitive economies globally based on their ability to create and maintain an environment that sustains the competitiveness of enterprises.
 
• **Singapore** returned to a leading position in the **2025** rankings, showcasing exceptional strength in **Business Efficiency** and **Economic Performance**. Its robust digital infrastructure and openness to **International Trade** were pivotal factors.
 
• **Switzerland** maintained its elite status in the top three, primarily due to its world-class **Infrastructure**, high-quality **Education system**, and stable **Government Efficiency**. It continues to lead in categories related to **Scientific Infrastructure** and **Institutional Framework**.
 
• **Hong Kong** secured a spot in the top three economies, reflecting its resurgence as a global financial hub. The region demonstrated significant improvements in **International Investment** and **Tax Policy**, which bolstered its overall **Government Efficiency** score.
 
• The **2025** edition of the ranking evaluated a total of **67 global economies**, providing a comprehensive benchmark for policymakers and business leaders to assess national performance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The IMD World Competitiveness Center:**
 
 
• It is a research group at the **International Institute for Management Development (IMD)** located in **Lausanne, Switzerland**. It has been publishing these rankings annually since **1989**.
 
• The ranking is widely regarded as one of the most authoritative reports on the competitiveness of nations, focusing on how nations manage their resources and competencies to increase prosperity.
 
 
 
• **The Four Pillars of Competitiveness:**
 
 
• **Economic Performance:** Evaluates the domestic economy, **International Trade**, **International Investment**, **Employment**, and **Prices**.
 
• **Government Efficiency:** Measures **Public Finance**, **Tax Policy**, **Institutional Framework**, **Business Legislation**, and **Societal Framework**.
 
• **Business Efficiency:** Assesses **Productivity and Efficiency**, **Labor Market**, **Finance**, **Management Practices**, and **Attitudes and Values**.
 
• **Infrastructure:** Looks at **Basic Infrastructure**, **Technological Infrastructure**, **Scientific Infrastructure**, **Health and Environment**, and **Education**.
 
 
 
• **Methodology and Data:**
 
 
• The ranking utilizes a combination of **Hard Data** (representing about **two-thirds** of the weight), which includes statistical indicators from international and national sources, and **Soft Data** (representing **one-third** of the weight) from an **Executive Opinion Survey**.
 
• In **2025**, the criteria were updated to reflect emerging global trends such as **Artificial Intelligence (AI) adoption**, **Energy Security**, and **Geopolitical Stability**.
 
 
 
• **Significance for Global Markets:**
 
 
• Economies like **Denmark**, **Ireland**, and **Sweden** often fluctuate within the top ten, highlighting the competitive nature of **European** markets compared to **Asian** powerhouses.
 
• The **2025** rankings specifically highlighted how "small" economies often outperform larger ones like the **USA** or **China** due to their **Agility** and specialized **Economic Policies**.
